content: Fridge/freezer does not operate. Fridge/freezer temperature is warm. Power cord is not plugged in properly; Temperature control is not set correctly; Refrigerator is located near a heat source or direct sunlight; Not enough clearance between refrigerator and sides/rear; The Vacation function is activated; The refrigerator is overloaded. Food is blocking the refrigerator vents. 1. Properly plug in the power cord. 2. Set the temperature lower. 3. Keep the refrigerator away from direct sunlight or a heat source. 4. Make sure there are at least 5 cm from the rear and sides. 5. Deactivate the Vacation function. 6. Do not overload the refrigerator. Do not allow food to block ventilation.

metadata.symptom: Fridge/freezer does not operate. Fridge/freezer temperature is warm.
metadata.possible_cause: Power cord is not plugged in properly; Temperature control is not set correctly; Refrigerator is located near a heat source or direct sunlight; Not enough clearance between refrigerator and sides/rear; The Vacation function is activated; The refrigerator is overloaded. Food is blocking the refrigerator vents.
metadata.solution:
1. Properly plug in the power cord.
2. Set the temperature lower.
3. Keep the refrigerator away from direct sunlight or a heat source.
4. Make sure there are at least 5 cm from the rear and sides.
5. Deactivate the Vacation function.
6. Do not overload the refrigerator. Do not allow food to block ventilation.

content: The SmartThings app fails to operate. 1. The SmartThings app is available for applicable models only. 2. The old Samsung Smart Refrigerator app cannot connect with Samsung Smart Home models.

content: The SmartThings app is installed but is not connected to my refrigerator. 1. You must log into your Samsung account to use the app. 2. Make sure that your router is operating normally. 3. If the Wi-Fi icon on the refrigerator’s display is off, this indicates that no network connection has been established yet. In this case, use the SmartThings app to connect and register your refrigerator to the access point (AP) of your house.

2. Make sure that your router is operating normally.
3. If the Wi-Fi icon on the refrigerator’s display is off, this indicates that no network connection has been established yet. In this case, use the SmartThings app to connect and register your refrigerator to the access point (AP) of your house.

content: Could not log into the app. 1. You must log into your Samsung account to use the app. 2. If you don’t have a Samsung account, follow the app’s onscreen instructions to create one.

content: The SmartThings app is successfully connected to my refrigerator but does not run. 1. Exit and restart the SmartThings app, or disconnect and reconnect the router. 2. Power off the refrigerator, and then power it on again after 1 minute.

metadata.solution:

2. Power off the refrigerator, and then power it on again after 1 minute.

content: The Wi-Fi icon is blinking. 1. Connect your refrigerator with the SmartThings app before use. When the connection is made successfully, the indicator stops blinking. 2. If you fail to make connection or don’t want to use the app, press and hold the button for 10 seconds. The indicator stops blinking with "O FF" shown on the temperature display.

metadata.symptom: The Wi-Fi icon is blinking.
metadata.solution:
1. Connect your refrigerator with the SmartThings app before use. When the connection is made successfully, the indicator stops blinking.
2. If you fail to make connection or don’t want to use the app, press and hold the button for 10 seconds. The indicator stops blinking with "O FF" shown on the temperature display.
